verdict.rationale: Datalab documents converting documents into structured, machine-readable Markdown, HTML, or JSON, and says Marker 'handles complex layouts,' which implies some structure preservation. It never explicitly documents heading hierarchy, section nesting, or reading-order guarantees. One hands-on report says Marker 'intermingled some columns in tricky cases,' a concrete reading-order flaw in edge layouts rather than a contradiction of an explicit claim. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of heading/section hierarchy in output, a documented reading-order capability, JSON block-structure details, and independent corroboration that structure survives on complex multi-column documents.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, parsed output preserves document hierarchy — headings, sections, reading order — so downstream LLMs see structure, not soup

citations.quote: Marker handles complex layouts, tables, math, and images.
Datalab provides document intelligence APIs to convert PDFs, spreadsheets, and images into structured, machine-readable outputs.
